observations: Murine allogeneic skin-graft study assessed early KC/CXCL1, MIP-1α/CCL3, and MIP-1β/CCL4 expression and production.

entities.name: NK-cell chemokine amplification
observations: In murine allogeneic skin grafts, recipient NK-cell depletion with anti-asialo GM1 or anti-NK1.1 reduced early KC/CXCL1, MIP-1α/CCL3, and MIP-1β/CCL4 mRNA by about 60–70% and reduced day-4 protein; day-2 mRNA was similar to isografts, whereas allograft mRNA remained elevated at day 3.

The early response occurred in athymic nude recipients, suggesting it did not require T cells; findings support NK-cell amplification, though evidence came from depletion experiments in one primary study.
